author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Coffee traders are preparing large deliveries of Brazilian arabica to ICE exchange warehouses, a move that could more than double certified stocks from 26-year lows and place downward pressure on benchmark prices, Reuters reported.

Market participants are seeking to certify at least 300,000 60-kilogram bags for delivery against the December futures contract. ICE-certified inventories have fallen below 220,000 bags after harvest delays and extreme weather disrupted supplies. More than 62,000 Brazilian bags had already reached depots for grading and quality checks.

Brazilian coffee exports to Belgium jumped 245.3% from a year earlier in August to 31,500 metric tons, government data analyzed by Terra Investimentos showed. Much of ICE’s available arabica is stored in Antwerp, making those shipments an important signal of possible exchange supply.

Certification is not automatic, and it remains unclear how many bags will pass inspection. Even the full expected volume would leave stocks below the roughly 1 million bags traders regard as comfortable. Still, rising inventories can influence algorithmic funds and physical-market expectations, making the delivery pipeline a closely watched commodity-market development.
dek: Traders are seeking to certify at least 300,000 bags of Brazilian arabica as ICE inventories sit near 26-year lows.
headline: Large coffee shipments could rebuild exchange stocks
